## Solution

**Claim:** $C^1[a,b]$ is **not** a closed subset of $C[a,b]$ under the supremum metric $d_\infty(f,g)=\sup_{x\in[a,b]}|f(x)-g(x)|$.

**Proof.** It suffices to exhibit a sequence $(f_n)_{n\ge 1}\subset C^1[a,b]$ that converges uniformly to some $f\in C[a,b]\setminus C^1[a,b]$, since uniform convergence is exactly convergence in the supremum metric, and a closed set must contain all its limit points.

Take $[a,b]=[-1,1]$ (the construction adapts to any interval containing $0$ in its interior; for a general interval one translates/rescales). Define

$$
f_n(x)=\sqrt{x^2+\tfrac{1}{n}},\qquad n\ge 1.
$$

Each $f_n$ is smooth on $\mathbb{R}$, hence $f_n\in C^1[-1,1]$.

**Uniform convergence to $|x|$.** For every $x\in[-1,1]$,

$$
\bigl|f_n(x)-|x|\bigr|=\sqrt{x^2+\tfrac{1}{n}}-\sqrt{x^2}=\frac{1/n}{\sqrt{x^2+\tfrac{1}{n}}+\sqrt{x^2}}.
$$

The denominator satisfies $\sqrt{x^2+1/n}+\sqrt{x^2}\ge \sqrt{1/n}=1/\sqrt{n}$, so

$$
\bigl|f_n(x)-|x|\bigr|\le \frac{1/n}{1/\sqrt{n}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}.
$$

The right-hand side is independent of $x$, so

$$
d_\infty(f_n,|\,\cdot\,|)=\sup_{x\in[-1,1]}\bigl|f_n(x)-|x|\bigr|\le \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}0.
$$

Thus $f_n\to|\,\cdot\,|$ in the supremum metric.

**The limit is not in $C^1[-1,1]$.** The function $f(x)=|x|$ is continuous on $[-1,1]$, so $f\in C[-1,1]$. However, $f$ is not differentiable at $x=0$ (the left derivative is $-1$ and the right derivative is $+1$), so $f\notin C^1[-1,1]$.

**Conclusion.** We have produced a sequence in $C^1[-1,1]$ converging in the supremum metric to a point of $C[-1,1]\setminus C^1[-1,1]$. Therefore $C^1[-1,1]$ fails to contain all its limit points and is **not closed** in $C[-1,1]$.

**Remark (general $[a,b]$).** For an arbitrary interval $[a,b]$, pick an interior point $c\in(a,b)$ and set $g_n(x)=\sqrt{(x-c)^2+1/n}$. The identical estimate gives $g_n\to|x-c|$ uniformly on $[a,b]$, with $g_n\in C^1[a,b]$ and $|x-c|\in C[a,b]\setminus C^1[a,b]$. Hence the conclusion holds on every non-degenerate interval. $\blacksquare$

### PROOF COMPLETE
